findings: Gaussian explicit/weighted-mean representations agree; accumulated independent-noise precision is retained.
Current native prior weight scales with observation count; fused-noise scaling can further increase smoothing.
With true fixed geometry, an independently stationary human-face crop still loses to a fixed Lucky strategy; lower objective can have higher image error.
In 16 independent evaluation repetitions, native four-frame mean retains the expected noise reduction; matched-family BM3D does not repair the F5 face bias.
F5 wins the color-edge and chromatic-texture controls. The failure is content-dependent, not a universal loss of burst information.
decision: Next change is limited to an explicit summed-likelihood plus scene-prior convention, separating prior strength from its robust transition and calibrating them together. No new texture/colour protection rule.
scope: Three small development crops, not independent scene-generalization or real-image acceptance.
96 noise-repetition references were rechecked at a standardized fixed-barrier gradient below 1e-6.
Matched BM3D uses separately measured PSDs; global stationarity is an approximation.
